oneLine: The physical yard outside the walls: who passed the gate, where each trailer is, who moves it, and what is done at the door.

rows.title: Check a truck in at the gate
rows.story: The gate clerk records a visit and its trailers. The seal is compared with the booking, and each trailer gets a move: to its door if on time and the door is free, otherwise to a spot. Site policy can turn a seal mismatch or a suspended carrier away.
reads: Yard spots and doors (copy from facility-layout)

then.does: marks the appointment as arrived: early, on time or late
stores the gate arrival, the start of the dock-to-stock clock
opens a case when the seal does not match

rows.title: Turn a truck away at the gate
rows.story: The gate clerk refuses a visit and records the reason. The refused visit is recorded as rejected and gets no trailer.

then.does: cancels the booked appointment with the reason 'turned away'
opens a case for the rejected visit

rows.title: Ask for a trailer to be moved
rows.story: A yard supervisor asks for a trailer to go to a spot or a door. The destination is checked and reserved. The yard also asks by itself: it calls the next trailer in when a door frees up and clears a dropped trailer after door work.
reads: Yard spots and doors (copy from facility-layout)

rows.title: Hand the next move to a yard-truck driver
rows.story: A hostler (yard-truck driver) asks for work. The yard picks the most urgent waiting move and lends it for a limited time. The trailer leaves its place at once; leaving a door frees that door.

then.does: completes the appointment when its trailer leaves the door

rows.title: Park or dock the trailer
rows.story: The hostler reports where the trailer was left. The move ends and the trailer is parked on a spot or docked at a door, in one step. An occupied place is refused and the move stays open.
reads: Yard spots and doors (copy from facility-layout)

then.does: moves the booking to the door the trailer really took, if different
attaches the trailer to the load at that door and starts loading

rows.title: Start work at the door
rows.story: A dock operator starts unloading or loading a docked trailer. If the site asks for it, an unsecured trailer is refused, and so is loading before a required inspection has passed.

rows.title: Secure a docked trailer
rows.story: A dock operator records that the trailer is held to the dock by a vehicle restraint or wheel chocks. It must be docked and have no open move.

rows.title: Finish unloading when the receipt closes
rows.story: inbound-receiving closes a receipt. When every ASN on a docked trailer has a closed receipt, its door work is completed and the trailer counts as empty. Staff can also complete door work by hand.
rows.policy: Whenever the last receipt of a docked trailer closes, complete its door work

then.does: keeps the door-work completion for its load adherence view

rows.title: Release the securing before the trailer leaves
rows.story: A dock operator frees the trailer from restraint or chocks. This is needed before it can leave its door, and is refused while door work is in progress.

rows.title: Inspect a trailer
rows.story: An inspector works through a checklist and completes it. If a required item fails, the inspection fails and the trailer is put on hold in the same step.

rows.title: Release a hold on a trailer
rows.story: A yard supervisor lifts the hold on a trailer, whether it was placed by hand, by a broken seal or by a failed inspection.

rows.title: Check a truck out of the yard
rows.story: The gate clerk lets the visit leave with the trailers it takes. Each must be on site and released, and an inspection before departure may be required. A trailer left behind is a drop and stays.

then.does: confirms the shipment and issues the bill of lading when the load is closed
completes the appointment when its trailer leaves the door

rows.title: Free the yard when a booking falls through
rows.story: dock-scheduling reports a booking cancelled, missed or moved to another door. The yard cancels the open moves that were bringing a trailer to that door. A trailer already on site stays where it is.
rows.policy: Whenever a booking is cancelled, missed or moved, cancel its open hostler moves to the door

rows.title: Take back moves whose lease ran out
rows.story: A sweep looks for claimed moves whose time ran out. Each goes back to the waiting list and its trailer back to where it was, unless that place was taken meanwhile.
rows.policy: Every sweep, put each claimed move whose lease has expired back on the waiting list

rows.title: Chase trailers that stay too long
rows.story: A sweep finds trailers on site whose time reached the limit for their kind and raises one alert for each.
rows.policy: Every sweep, raise a dwell alert once for each trailer past its limit

then.does: opens a case for the overdue trailer

rows.title: Audit the yard against the records
rows.story: A supervisor walks the yard, notes what is at each place, then closes the check. It reports every difference from what the yard believes. A place not seen is missing if a trailer should be there.

then.does: opens one case per difference; a clean check opens none

hotspots.text: A door closure or a retired slot under a trailer already there is not handled. Closures only guard arrival. Handling the case is left to a later phase.
Hazmat and reefer rules trust the declared load. The yard cannot check what a trailer holds, and one classified after parking stays where it is.
Securing, release and inspection results are published but nobody reads them yet.
The event contract does not yet declare who made a change when an agent writes through the tool interface. The data is on the wire.

opportunities.text: exception-management is the planned reader of failed inspections, so that a failure becomes an exception case to work.
A hazmat segregation rule, so classes may not stand on adjacent spots, needs spot neighbours that facility-layout does not publish yet. A later ADR is planned.
